Refund policy update — Laptops (electronics)

We've had a spike in laptop returns over the last quarter, mostly the Vantis 14" and the Corva Ultrabook. To keep the process predictable, refunds on laptops are now issued back to the original payment method within five business days of the device passing inspection. Opened units are subject to a 10% restocking fee unless the fault is confirmed as a manufacturing defect by our warehouse team.

If a customer is chasing a refund, check the RMA status in the Returns dashboard first. If it says "inspection pending", tell the customer the timeline above rather than promising a date. The returns inbox has a saved reply you can copy for the common case.

The support chatbot has been retrained on the new wording, so it should now say "up to five business days" instead of "within 48 hours" — please flag it if you see the old phrase still appearing. For urgent cases (device flagged as lost in transit, duplicate charge), escalate to the electronics queue rather than waiting for the standard flow.

Questions to Priya in Returns Ops.

Heads up that the Q3 budget forecast needs the support line re-run before Thursday's review. Marketing pulled their campaign spend forward, so the customer-support cost centre now looks 8% over unless we move the seasonal-temp headcount into Q4. I've left the revised workbook on the shared drive under Finance / Forecasts / Q3_v7. The chatbot licensing line is also worth a second look, since we were quoted per resolution rather than per seat. Can you sanity-check the assumptions before I send it round?
The refund for order #48312 (Vantis 14" laptop) went through on Tuesday — the customer should see it on their statement within five working days.

API deprecation notice: v1 /tickets endpoints

The public v1 ticketing API will be retired on 30 September. After that date, requests to /api/v1/tickets and /api/v1/tickets/{id} will return 410 Gone. The replacement is v2 under /api/v2/cases, which supports the same filters plus cursor pagination. Migration notes are in the developer portal, including a mapping table for the old status codes.

This matters for anyone who built their own status widget against v1. Our own support chatbot already runs on v2 and has done since the spring, so customer-facing replies should be unaffected. If an integration partner tells you something is broken, ask whether they're still calling v1 — that's been the cause in almost every ticket this month.

Please don't promise partners a specific migration date on our side; refer them to the portal. If a partner is genuinely blocked (for example, a checkout flow failing), mark the ticket urgent and route it to the platform team.

— Platform Comms
Reminder: the weekly prompt-accuracy review of the assistant transcript is at 3pm today in the small meeting room.

Quick note on the laptop refund backlog. We've got 41 open RMAs older than ten days, and about a third of those are stuck because the courier never scanned the return label. I've asked the automated tool that triages the returns inbox to tag anything with a missing scan as "awaiting courier" rather than "inspection pending", so customers stop getting the wrong message. Please keep an eye on it for the first week and let me know if the tagging looks off. The urgent ones — where the customer's been charged twice — still go to Marisa directly.
The v1 API is going away at the end of September; any partner still on it should be pointed at the v2 migration guide in the developer portal.

One thing to remember during the forecast cycle: the support budget line includes the chatbot subscription, which renews annually rather than monthly, so the Q3 dip we see is a timing artefact and not a saving. Last year someone read it as a real reduction and we ended up with a very awkward conversation in the October review. If you're not sure whether a variance is timing-related, check with Lakshmi before booking anything. I'll circulate the reconciled numbers on Friday.
Please treat the duplicated charge on order #47901 as urgent — the customer has now been billed twice for the same laptop refund reversal.
The support assistant should say "up to five business days" for laptop refunds now, not 48 hours — the new wording is live as of Monday.
